lesson.menu_title: A Week in the Sales Team
lesson.menu_desc: Reading about a normal work week, and asking how often -- 34 slides
lesson.subtitle: Lesson 2 -- A Week in the Sales Team
lesson.title_tag: Professor View -- Fernanda Bassani Rubio | Lesson 2 -- A Week in the Sales Team
lesson.grammar_point: present simple questions with do and does and adverbs of frequency

listenings.text: Hi, I am Priya. I am a sales coordinator in Pune, in India. My week is very regular. On Monday I always have two meetings: one with my team and one with the global team. On Tuesday and Wednesday I usually prepare quotes for our customers. I often follow up by phone, because many customers do not read long emails. I sometimes visit a factory, maybe once a month. On Friday I send the sales report to my manager. I never send it late, because my manager reads it on Friday afternoon. And the forecast? We update it every month, on the last Thursday.

Good morning. My name is Julien, and I am a purchasing manager in Lyon, in France. We make car seats, and we buy adhesives from three suppliers. How often do I place an order? Usually every two weeks, on Tuesday. Before I place an order, I always ask for a quote. I compare the prices, and then I decide. Do I visit my suppliers? Not often. Maybe two times a year. But I like it when a supplier follows up after a quote. It shows me that they care. And please, never send a quote after the deadline. I do not read it.

reading.rtitle: Meet the Team: Automotive Sales, Brazil
paras: Our automotive team in Brazil is small, but it is busy. There are five people, and they deal with some of our biggest car makers. The week always starts with the weekly meeting on Monday at nine. The team looks at new orders, open quotes and the problems of the week. The meeting is usually short: thirty minutes, never more than an hour.

From Tuesday to Thursday, the team works with customers. They send quotes, answer questions and follow up after every call. Each person has one or two customer visits a month. After a visit, they always write a short email the same day. Our customers place an order every week or every two weeks, so the team checks the orders every morning.

Friday is for numbers. The team sends the sales report to the director before twelve. Once a month, they also update the forecast for the next three months. The deadline for the forecast is the last Thursday of the month. Is it a lot of work? Yes. But the team says the rhythm helps: everybody knows what happens on each day.
reading.source: Alumni by Better -- A2 reading, written for this lesson from a common sales-team routine
